2:1.sourceText: Ἐγένοντο δὲ καὶ ψευδοπροφῆται ἐν τῷ λαῷ, ὡς καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν ἔσονται ψευδοδιδάσκαλοι, οἵτινες παρεισάξουσιν αἱρέσεις ἀπωλείας, καὶ τὸν ἀγοράσαντα αὐτοὺς δεσπότην ἀρνούμενοι, ἐπάγοντες ἑαυτοῖς ταχινὴν ἀπώλειαν·
2:1.targetText: But there also came false prophets among the people, as there will also be false teachers among you, who will stealthily bring in destructive sects, even denying the Master who bought them, bringing quick destruction to themselves,

groups.note: The actual genitive destruction noun qualifies the sects/opinions, rendered adjectivally as destructive; the written source is not a distinct destructive adjective.

2:2.sourceText: καὶ πολλοὶ ἐξακολουθήσουσιν αὐτῶν ταῖς ἀσελγείαις, δι’ οὓς ἡ ὁδὸς τῆς ἀληθείας βλασφημηθήσεται·
2:2.targetText: and many will follow out their destructive ways, because of whom the way of the truth will be spoken of [as] evil,

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.
N1904 has ἀσελγείαις, licentious/debauched acts, whereas LSV gives destructive ways. The different written moral-action and destruction readings are not treated as exact lexical counterparts.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV follows a destruction/pernicious-ways reading where pinned N1904 writes licentiousnesses, ἀσελγείαις. The actual differing head remains explicit.

2:3.sourceText: καὶ ἐν πλεονεξίᾳ πλαστοῖς λόγοις ὑμᾶς ἐμπορεύσονται· οἷς τὸ κρίμα ἔκπαλαι οὐκ ἀργεῖ, καὶ ἡ ἀπώλεια αὐτῶν οὐ νυστάζει.
2:3.targetText: and in covetousness, with forged words, they will make merchandise of you, whose judgment of old is not idle, and their destruction does not slumber.

groups.note: The actual dative relative names those for whom the judgment is intended. English recasts that recipient relation possessively as whose judgment; the source is not relabeled as a written Greek genitive relative.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

2:4.sourceText: εἰ γὰρ ὁ Θεὸς ἀγγέλων ἁμαρτησάντων οὐκ ἐφείσατο, ἀλλὰ σειροῖς ζόφου ταρταρώσας παρέδωκεν εἰς κρίσιν τηρουμένους,
2:4.targetText: For if God did not spare messengers having sinned, but having cast [them] down to Tartarus with chains of deepest gloom, delivered [them], having been reserved to judgment,

groups.note: The actual messengers are the same spared-not, Tartarus-cast and handed-over group. English resumes those stated messengers as the two bracketed them objects; no independent additional Greek pronouns are claimed.
The actual genitive gloom noun ζόφου supplies the darkness qualifier. English deepest expresses the noun’s dense-gloom sense, not an independently written Greek superlative adjective.
The actual Greek τηρουμένους is a present passive keeping participle; LSV expresses it as having been reserved. The same retained group remains linked with that aspect/form difference explicit.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

The actual pinned σειροῖς belongs to σιρός, pits/dungeons, not the different chains/cords noun σειρά with dative plural σειραῖς. N1904 already supplies lemma σιρός; neither the source spelling nor its metadata is changed to manufacture an English chains match.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV has chains, following the σειραῖς/σειρά reading, while pinned N1904 writes σειροῖς, pits/dungeons. The distinct enclosure and restraint nouns remain unpaired, including the English with that belongs to this different construction.

review.note: The pits/chains difference is lexical and textual, not a synonym substitution. The actual N1904 concordance already identifies σιρός, with source variant Strong string 04577. No metadata correction or Greek text alteration is made. NET note18 and the primary lexicons distinguish σιροῖς/σειροῖς pits from σειραῖς chains.

2:5.sourceText: καὶ ἀρχαίου κόσμου οὐκ ἐφείσατο, ἀλλὰ ὄγδοον Νῶε δικαιοσύνης κήρυκα ἐφύλαξεν, κατακλυσμὸν κόσμῳ ἀσεβῶν ἐπάξας,
2:5.targetText: and did not spare the old world, but kept the eighth person, Noah, a preacher of righteousness, having brought a flood on the world of the impious,

2:6.sourceText: καὶ πόλεις Σοδόμων καὶ Γομόρρας τεφρώσας καταστροφῇ κατέκρινεν, ὑπόδειγμα μελλόντων ἀσεβεῖν τεθεικώς,
2:6.targetText: and having turned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to ashes, condemned with an overthrow, having set [them as] an example to those about to be impious,

groups.note: The actual cities are both turned to ashes/condemned and set as an example in the immediately coordinated judgment account. English resumes those same cities as them and states the predicative example relation with as, without an independently written second object or as preposition.

targetPhrases.text: to those about to be impious

groups.note: The actual prospective μελλόντων governs the impious-acting infinitive ἀσεβεῖν. English expresses the whole future-person predicate as to those about to be impious; the be impious predicate belongs to the actual ἀσεβέω verb, not to μέλλω alone.

2:7.sourceText: καὶ δίκαιον Λὼτ καταπονούμενον ὑπὸ τῆς τῶν ἀθέσμων ἐν ἀσελγείᾳ ἀναστροφῆς ἐρύσατο,—
2:7.targetText: and He rescued righteous Lot, worn down by the conduct of the lawless in licentiousness,

2:8.sourceText: βλέμματι γὰρ καὶ ἀκοῇ ὁ δίκαιος ἐνκατοικῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς ἡμέραν ἐξ ἡμέρας ψυχὴν δικαίαν ἀνόμοις ἔργοις ἐβασάνιζεν,—
2:8.targetText: for the righteous [man] dwelling among them was tormented in [his] righteous soul, day by day, in seeing and hearing unlawful works—

groups.note: Greek actively states that the righteous man tormented his own righteous soul; English presents the same man’s inward distress as was tormented in his righteous soul. The full predicate/body-part construction is retained with this active-to-passive/locative recasting, not an invented external tormentor or separately written Greek passive form or possessive.

2:9.sourceText: οἶδεν Κύριος εὐσεβεῖς ἐκ πειρασμοῦ ῥύεσθαι, ἀδίκους δὲ εἰς ἡμέραν κρίσεως κολαζομένους τηρεῖν,
2:9.targetText: the LORD has known to rescue [the] pious out of temptation, and to keep [the] unrighteous being punished to [the] day of judgment,

2:10.sourceText: μάλιστα δὲ τοὺς ὀπίσω σαρκὸς ἐν ἐπιθυμίᾳ μιασμοῦ πορευομένους καὶ κυριότητος καταφρονοῦντας. τολμηταὶ, αὐθάδεις, δόξας οὐ τρέμουσιν βλασφημοῦντες,
2:10.targetText: and chiefly those following after the flesh in lust [and] defilement, and despising lordship. Bold, self-pleased, they are not afraid to speak evil of glorious ones,

groups.note: The actual genitive defilement noun qualifies lust, lust of defilement. English coordinates lust and defilement; the noun stays linked while its added conjunction is separately explained.

The actual trembling verb τρέμουσιν is rendered they are afraid in the feared-blasphemy construction. Its fear/trembling predicate remains actual; the source is not replaced with a different Greek φοβέομαι verb.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV supplies a conjunction between lust and defilement; N1904 has a genitive defilement qualifier rather than a written conjunction.

2:11.sourceText: ὅπου ἄγγελοι ἰσχύϊ καὶ δυνάμει μείζονες ὄντες οὐ φέρουσιν κατ’ αὐτῶν παρὰ Κυρίῳ βλάσφημον κρίσιν.
2:11.targetText: whereas messengers, being greater in strength and power, do not bear a slanderous judgment against them before the LORD;

2:12.sourceText: οὗτοι δέ, ὡς ἄλογα ζῷα γεγεννημένα φυσικὰ εἰς ἅλωσιν καὶ φθοράν, ἐν οἷς ἀγνοοῦσιν βλασφημοῦντες, ἐν τῇ φθορᾷ αὐτῶν καὶ φθαρήσονται,
2:12.targetText: and these, as irrational natural beasts, made to be caught and destroyed—in what things they are ignorant of, slandering—in their destruction will be destroyed;

groups.note: The actual perfect passive γεννάω participle denotes having been born; English uses made for the production of these creatures. It is not a separately written Greek making verb.

The actual goal preposition with capture and destruction nouns gives the creatures’ capture/destruction destination. English verbalizes that complete purpose as to be caught and destroyed, not independently written Greek catching/destroying infinitives or passive auxiliaries.

The actual dative relative under ἐν identifies the unknown matters; English expands this topic/object relation as what things ... of around the ignorance predicate. This does not claim a separately written Greek of preposition or a genitive relative form.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.
N1904 has an additive καί with the final destruction prediction; LSV has no separate and/also word there.

2:13.sourceText: ἀδικούμενοι μισθὸν ἀδικίας· ἡδονὴν ἡγούμενοι τὴν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ τρυφήν, σπίλοι καὶ μῶμοι ἐντρυφῶντες ἐν ταῖς ἀπάταις αὐτῶν συνευωχούμενοι ὑμῖν,
2:13.targetText: doing unjustly, [they will receive] a reward of unrighteousness, esteeming pleasure in the day, [and] luxury—[they are] spots and blemishes, reveling in their deceits, feasting with you,

unmappedSource.reason: The actual ἀδικούμενοι is nonactive, suffering wrong/harm in this adverse-recompense context. LSV gives active doing unjustly and supplies a separate receiving predicate. The patient/agent difference is not blurred by making the actual passive harm verb mean doing or receiving.
Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV actively describes the wrongdoing, while pinned N1904 has the nonactive suffering-harm/wrong participle; the unlike agency is explicit.
LSV supplies this future receiving predicate in brackets. N1904 has the actual nonactive suffering-harm expression with its wages, not a written future receiving verb.
English supplies coordination of pleasure and luxury; N1904 instead has considering the daytime luxury a pleasure.
English supplies a subject/copula to introduce the spots/blemishes apposition; no corresponding finite be verb is written.

review.note: The actual wages/unrighteousness nouns remain paired. The contextual connection between suffering harm as recompense and receiving a bad reward is explained, but no lexical identity is forced for the central passive suffering versus active doing/receiving distinction. LSJ and Mounce explicitly treat this participle as suffering harm/wrong.

2:14.sourceText: ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντες μεστοὺς μοιχαλίδος καὶ ἀκαταπαύστους ἁμαρτίας, δελεάζοντες ψυχὰς ἀστηρίκτους, καρδίαν γεγυμνασμένην πλεονεξίας ἔχοντες, κατάρας τέκνα·
2:14.targetText: having eyes full of adultery, and unable to cease from sin, enticing unstable souls, having a heart exercised in covetousnesses, children of a curse,

groups.note: The actual Greek image is eyes full of an adulteress, with a feminine-person noun. LSV interprets the whole desirous-gaze image as eyes full of adultery; this phrase-level interpretation does not assert an abstract μοίχεια noun or a general lexical rule that an adulteress means adultery.

N1904 has genitive singular greed/covetousness, πλεονεξίας; LSV gives in covetousnesses, reflecting a plural/domain rendering. The actual greed noun is retained with the number/case construction difference explicit, not an independently written Greek in preposition.

review.note: This is a whole eyes/full/adulteress phrase-level metonymy, not a source-witness change to an abstract adultery noun. Mounce explicitly supplies the metonymic lustful-appearance sense for this exact verse; NET also prints full of adultery while identifying the literal adulteress wording. The actual feminine-person lemma remains visible.

2:15.sourceText: καταλειπόντες εὐθεῖαν ὁδὸν ἐπλανήθησαν, ἐξακολουθήσαντες τῇ ὁδῷ τοῦ Βαλαὰμ τοῦ Βεώρ, ὃς μισθὸν ἀδικίας ἠγάπησεν,
2:15.targetText: having forsaken a right way, they went astray, having followed in the way of Balaam the [son] of Bosor, who loved a reward of unrighteousness,

unmappedSource.reason: The actual N1904 name is Beor, Βεώρ, with its genitive article. LSV instead has the Bosor genealogy/parent-name reading; this different written name link is not collapsed into an exact identity.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV names Bosor where pinned N1904 writes Beor. The different parent-name ancestry phrase remains explicit, rather than inferring one name from the other.

2:16.sourceText: ἔλεγξιν δὲ ἔσχεν ἰδίας παρανομίας· ὑποζύγιον ἄφωνον ἐν ἀνθρώπου φωνῇ φθεγξάμενον ἐκώλυσεν τὴν τοῦ προφήτου παραφρονίαν.
2:16.targetText: and had a rebuke of his own iniquity—a mute donkey, having spoken in man’s voice, forbid the madness of the prophet.

groups.note: The actual beast-of-burden noun ὑποζύγιον designates the donkey in the Balaam episode, rendered donkey. The source does not write a different ὄνος noun.

2:17.sourceText: οὗτοί εἰσιν πηγαὶ ἄνυδροι καὶ ὁμίχλαι ὑπὸ λαίλαπος ἐλαυνόμεναι, οἷς ὁ ζόφος τοῦ σκότους τετήρηται.
2:17.targetText: These are wells without water, and clouds driven by a storm, to whom the deepest gloom of darkness has been kept throughout the age;

groups.note: The actual dense-gloom noun ζόφος is expressed as deepest gloom. English deepest conveys that intensity; the Greek does not separately write a superlative adjective.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual N1904 weather noun is ὁμίχλαι, mists, whereas LSV gives clouds from a different cloud-noun reading. The distinct physical-designation heads are not silently substituted.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV names clouds where pinned N1904 has mists, ὁμίχλαι; their related weather image does not create exact lexical identity.
The final age-duration phrase is additional wording in LSV, absent from pinned N1904 at this reference.

2:18.sourceText: ὑπέρογκα γὰρ ματαιότητος φθεγγόμενοι δελεάζουσιν ἐν ἐπιθυμίαις σαρκὸς ἀσελγείαις τοὺς ὀλίγως ἀποφεύγοντας τοὺς ἐν πλάνῃ ἀναστρεφομένους,
2:18.targetText: for speaking swollen words of vanity, they entice in desires of the flesh—licentiousness, those who had truly escaped from those conducting themselves in error,

groups.note: N1904 has a present escaping participle; LSV describes a completed had escaped action. The real escape head remains linked while its aspect and the separate barely/truly difference are explicit.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual ὀλίγως means barely/scarcely, while LSV gives truly. These different degree/reality adverbs are not equated.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV truly differs from N1904 barely/scarcely, ὀλίγως. The actual escaping action remains linked separately with its present-versus-completed wording noted.

2:19.sourceText: ἐλευθερίαν αὐτοῖς ἐπαγγελλόμενοι, αὐτοὶ δοῦλοι ὑπάρχοντες τῆς φθορᾶς· ᾧ γάρ τις ἥττηται, τούτῳ δεδούλωται.
2:19.targetText: promising liberty to them, themselves being servants of corruption, for by whom anyone has been overcome, he has been brought to servitude to this one also;

targetPhrases.text: he has been brought to servitude

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds also to the concluding enslavement statement; no additive particle is written there in pinned N1904.

2:20.sourceText: εἰ γὰρ ἀποφυγόντες τὰ μιάσματα τοῦ κόσμου ἐν ἐπιγνώσει τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ Σωτῆρος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τούτοις δὲ πάλιν ἐμπλακέντες ἡττῶνται, γέγονεν αὐτοῖς τὰ ἔσχατα χείρονα τῶν πρώτων.
2:20.targetText: for if having escaped from the defilements of the world, in the acknowledging of the LORD and Savior Jesus Christ, and again being entangled by these things, they have been overcome, the last things have become worse to them than the first,

groups.note: The actual escaping-from compound supplies having escaped from and its defilement object relation; there is no independently written extra Greek from preposition.

The actual N1904 overcoming predicate is present passive, they are overcome; LSV gives perfect have been overcome. The same overcome people remain linked with this tense/aspect wording difference explicit.

2:21.sourceText: κρεῖττον γὰρ ἦν αὐτοῖς μὴ ἐπεγνωκέναι τὴν ὁδὸν τῆς δικαιοσύνης, ἢ ἐπιγνοῦσιν ὑποστρέψαι ἐκ τῆς παραδοθείσης αὐτοῖς ἁγίας ἐντολῆς.
2:21.targetText: for it were better to them not to have acknowledged the way of righteousness, than having acknowledged [it], to turn back from the holy command delivered to them,

groups.note: The actual way is the object of both not having known and the immediately contrasted having known circumstance. English repeats this same acknowledged way as bracketed [it], without a separately written second Greek object.

2:22.sourceText: συμβέβηκεν αὐτοῖς τὸ τῆς ἀληθοῦς παροιμίας Κύων ἐπιστρέψας ἐπὶ τὸ ἴδιον ἐξέραμα, καί Ὗς λουσαμένη εἰς κυλισμὸν βορβόρου.
2:22.targetText: and that of the true proverb has happened to them: “A dog turned back on his own vomit,” and, “A sow having bathed herself—to rolling in mire.”

groups.note: The actual aorist returning participle is expressed as the main past action of the quoted dog statement. The action remains actual while its English finite presentation is explicit.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds an opening conjunction before the proverb frame; N1904 begins directly with has happened.
